newsitem.title: CHINA: HK airport authority sees large offshore borrowing.
newsitem.headline: HK airport authority sees large offshore borrowing.

text.p: Hong Kong's Airport Authority (AA) plans to make its mark in offshore debt markets after Hong Kong's new airport takes off in early 1998.
"You will see our presence in the major overseas markets, including Yankee, Samurai and Euro markets," AA treasurer Hon-yung Wong told Reuters.
He said the Authority, which is overseeing the construction and financing of Chek Lap Kok Airport, will also seek a rating in the longer term, to facilitate international borrowings.

Even though the airport is expected to generate massive revenues, with capacity to process 35 million passengers and up to three million tonnes of cargo a year, the Authority plans no let-up in borrowing.
"Our future borrowing requirements will be huge," said Wong, speaking after announcing plans to raise HK$3 billion (US$387 million) through a three-year revolving credit facility.

Proceeds of the loan are earmarked for general corporate purposes, including a second runway and a concourse at Chek Lap Kok airport and new capital spending after the airport opens in April next year.
After the second runway's completion, passenger capacity is estimated to rise to about 87 million passengers and about nine million tonnes of cargo.
Wong said the AA plans to use both domestic and overseas borrowings to minimise cost of funds and ensure efficient treasury management, even though it would be cash rich.
"I think that is an admirable position to be in, and it should be the objective of every corporate treasurer," he said.
He said the AA had completed preparations for a note issuance facility (NIF) -- it is not yet signed -- to be arranged and managed by the Hong Kong Monetary Authority.
This facility would allow both fixed and floating-rate issuance, and would be a source of long-term cash, he said.
"We are more interested in ... five-, seven- and 10-year maturities," Wong said, adding that he expected the first issue to be launched in October "or thereabouts".
The AA would use the bank market for short-term funding -- three-months to five-year maturities, he added. "We can have access to the entire yield curve," he said.
In January 1996, the Authority signed a credit agreement with 48 banks for a five-year facility of HK$8.2 billion to finance Phase 1a of the airport project.
Loans drawn under that facility will be repaid in full by September 30, 2001.
Barring unforeseen circumstances, the Authority expects that facility to be sufficient for Phase 1a, and drawdown will begin in October this year. ($ = 7.747 Hong Kong Dollars)
